summary:
Shin Saimdang (1504–1551) was a Joseon-era Korean artist, writer, calligrapher, and poet, born in Gangneung. Educated in literature and Neo-Confucianism, she became known for delicate paintings of plants, insects, and landscapes. She continued developing her talents after marriage, despite the limited opportunities for women of her time. She was the mother of scholar Yi I and is often presented as an ideal Confucian mother.

In 2009, she became the first woman depicted on a South Korean banknote, the 50,000-won note. The choice was intended to honor her artistic achievements and role in education, but feminist critics argued that it reinforced traditional expectations of women as wives and mothers.
